name: Louisville Muhammad Ali International Airport
before:
Louisville's airport, and one where the name is misleading. Despite being called an international airport it has no regularly scheduled international passenger flights at all. It is a port of entry, and what comes through it is freight.

That freight is enormous. UPS runs its Worldport hub here, which makes Louisville the third busiest cargo airport in the United States behind Anchorage and Memphis, and sixth in the world. Nearly 6.6 billion pounds of cargo passed through in 2024, against 4.8 million passengers.

The passenger side is straightforward. The Jerry E. Abramson Terminal has 24 gates across two concourses joined by a rotunda, with ground transport and baggage claim on the first floor and ticketing above.

The code SDF comes from Standiford Field, the airport's old name. It was renamed in 2019 after Muhammad Ali, a Louisville native, three years after his death.

The Kentucky Air National Guard flies C-130s from the co-located base.
after:
Louisville's airport, and one where the name is misleading. Despite being called an international airport, it has no scheduled international passenger flights: every nonstop route on the airport's own list is to a US city.

UPS runs its worldwide air hub, Worldport, at the airport, which makes Louisville one of the busiest cargo airports in the world. In 2025 it was one of the two busiest in the United States, handling nearly 7.5 billion pounds of cargo and mail against about 4.6 million passengers.

On the passenger side, the Jerry E. Abramson Terminal has two concourses, A and B, joined by a rotunda.

The airport was called Standiford Field until 1995, and the code SDF did not change when it was renamed in 2019 after Muhammad Ali, a Louisville native.

Kentucky Air National Guard C-130s fly from the co-located base.

claims.note: The drafting team asked for the current position from the airport authority. Its destinations page (read 23 Sep 2026) lists 41 nonstop destinations, every one in the United States, and the airline-by-airline tab of the same page (op-destinations-raw) is domestic too, including the Sun Country casino charters to Atlantic City, Gulfport-Biloxi, Laughlin, New Orleans and Reno. The operator's 2025 statistics list only US airlines carrying scheduled passengers (American, Delta, Southwest, United and their regional partners, Allegiant, Spirit, Breeze, Sun Country). 'Regularly' and 'at all' dropped as padding.

claims.claim: one of the busiest cargo airports in the world
claims.inAfter: which makes Louisville one of the busiest cargo airports in the world
claims.note: Was 'sixth in the world'. Good sources give different world ranks for different years and measures: Wikipedia sixth; the operator fifth for 2024 (ACI's World Airport Traffic Report); the operator's April 2026 release 'top three' for 2025 on ACI's loaded-and-unloaded measure excluding transit, while ACI's own April 2026 release names Anchorage third on its headline cargo ranking. No single rank is supported by two sources, so the text says what all of them support.

sources.quote: It is also the world's sixth-busiest airport by cargo traffic

In 2025, SDF is the no. 1 busiest airport in North America and top three in the world for total loaded and unloaded cargo that excludes transit freight as shown in ACI World's preliminary World Airport Traffic Report.

claims.claim: in 2025 one of the two busiest cargo airports in the United States
claims.inAfter: In 2025 it was one of the two busiest in the United States
claims.note: Was 'the third busiest cargo airport in the United States behind Anchorage and Memphis'. Both 2026 sources put Louisville ahead of Memphis in 2025. The FAA's preliminary CY2025 all-cargo landed-weight table (9 July 2026) ranks it second in the US, behind Anchorage, with Memphis third and down 23.3 per cent; in 2024 Memphis was ahead (21.2 billion lb against 18.0 billion). The operator, citing ACI's preliminary 2025 report, calls it first in North America on loaded and unloaded cargo excluding transit, and says it surpassed Memphis for the first time. First or second depends on the measure (Anchorage's cargo is largely transit), so the text says one of the two busiest.
